title: Rehearsing the band at Ciro's and starting to conduct from the drums
summary: Lee rehearsed Nat's band when Nat was away, and Nat began having Lee conduct from the drums.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But before Cyros, though, we went to Las Vegas, I think, the first big one he played was Rancho Vegas -- El Rancho Vegas. That was still during the time when you couldn't live on the Strip. You had to live on the west side. Well, we played Rancho Vegas, and we came from Vegas, came back to L.A. to open at Cyros, and Nat had to go do a radio show. And he said, "Lee, get all the music out, and I'll be back around 4:30 or 4:00 o'clock." And there was a 1:00 o'clock rehearsal, so I rehearsed the band.
And when he came back, I was leaving and he was coming in, and he said, "Hey, where you going?" You know, and I told him, "I'm going home to have dinner." And he said, "Well,

what about the band?" I said, "I rehearsed the band". And he said, "Well, you didn't know what I wanted to do -- how could you rehearse the band?" And I said "I rehearsed everything you had in the book; you can do whatever you want to do."

But I was tired of staying all day for rehearsals because it's like any other star, I guess -- he'd play around and tell jokes with the band, when he'd meet the new musicians and all this. And I'll never forget in Vegas, we went to rehearse at 1 o'clock, and they opened the house on us at 7:30, and we were still there trying to rehearse, but that's from telling jokes, and really having fun with the musicians.
But anyway, that's how I started conducting.

Yeah, I started conducting for him, because after I rehearsed at that time, you know, he saw that we got through in a hurry, and then I started conducting for him. I would conduct from the drums -- the drums always sat right down in front of the band, and I conducted all over the country for him. We -- in '53, also, after I joined him, we went to - and in March of '54 -- we went abroad, you know, and we got to London, we were gonna play the Palladium and they didn't want John Collins and Charlie Harris and myself -- John Collins was the guitarist, and you know, Charlie Harris was on bass, and they said we couldn't appear with him at the Palladium.
